data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.title: advise
sections.question: advise
sections.summary: to tell someone what you think they should do

senses.definition: to tell someone what you think they should do in a particular situation
examples: The doctor advised her to rest for a week and drink plenty of water.
He advised his friend to look for a new job.

answers.answer: The doctor advised her to rest for a week and drink plenty of water.
He advised his new shirt with the blue trousers to look smart.
She advised the front door shut because the room was getting too cold.
He advised his lunch quickly because he only had fifteen minutes to eat.

sections.title: agree
sections.question: agree
sections.summary: to have the same opinion as someone; to say yes to something

senses.definition: to have the same opinion as someone else, or to say yes to something
examples: She agreed with her friend that the new restaurant was excellent.
They agreed to meet at the café at three o'clock.

answers.answer: She agreed with her friend that the new restaurant was excellent.
He agreed his coat on the chair and sat down for the meeting.
She agreed the window open to let some fresh air into the warm room.
He agreed his lunch in the kitchen every morning before going to school.

sections.title: apologize
sections.question: apologize
sections.summary: to tell someone that you are sorry for doing something wrong

senses.definition: to tell someone that you are sorry for something wrong you have done
examples: She apologized to her friend for arriving late to the birthday party.
He apologized for the mistake and promised it would not happen again.

answers.answer: He apologized to his sister for forgetting her birthday last week.
She apologized her keys on the table before going upstairs to bed.
He apologized the television when he walked into the sitting room.
She apologized her new shoes to see if they felt comfortable on her feet.

sections.title: ask
sections.question: ask
sections.summary: to say something to someone as a question to get information or a response

senses.definition: to say or write something to someone to get information or a reply
examples: She asked the teacher to explain the homework one more time.
He asked his friend if she wanted to come to the party.

answers.answer: She asked the teacher to explain the homework question one more time.
He asked the soup before adding more salt and pepper to it.
She asked the door to find out if anyone was waiting inside the room.
He asked his shoes on carefully before leaving the house for school.

sections.title: compliment
sections.question: compliment
sections.summary: to say something nice to someone about their appearance, work, or behaviour

senses.definition: to say something nice to someone about their appearance, work, or behaviour
examples: She complimented her colleague on the excellent presentation he gave.
He complimented his sister on her beautiful new dress.

senses.definition: a remark that expresses praise or admiration
examples: She was very happy when her boss paid her a compliment about her work.

answers.answer: She complimented her colleague on the excellent presentation he gave to the team.
He complimented the soup by adding more salt and pepper before serving it.
She complimented the door shut because the music next door was too loud.
He complimented his keys into his bag before leaving the house for work.

sections.title: congratulate
sections.question: congratulate
sections.summary: to tell someone you are pleased about their success or good news

senses.definition: to tell someone that you are pleased because they have done something well or something good has happened to them
examples: She congratulated her sister on passing her driving test.
His friends congratulated him on getting a new job.

answers.answer: She congratulated her sister on passing her driving test first time.
He congratulated the pasta for ten minutes until it was perfectly cooked.
She congratulated the window to let some cool air into the hot room.
He congratulated his homework and handed it to the teacher at the start of class.

sections.title: disagree
sections.question: disagree
sections.summary: to have a different opinion from someone else

senses.definition: to have a different opinion from someone else and not be able to agree
examples: She disagreed with her brother about which film to watch that evening.
The two teachers disagreed about the best way to teach grammar.

answers.answer: She disagreed with her brother about which film to watch that evening.
He disagreed the door and walked into the empty room on his own.
She disagreed the table before everyone sat down for the dinner party.
He disagreed his coat and hung it carefully by the front door.

sections.title: greet
sections.question: greet
sections.summary: to welcome someone with words or actions when you first meet them

senses.definition: to welcome someone with words or actions when you meet them
examples: She greeted her guests at the door with a big smile and a warm hello.
He greeted his old friend with a hug when she arrived at the station.

answers.answer: She greeted her old friend with a big hug when she arrived at the station.
He greeted a cup of coffee and read the newspaper all morning.
She greeted the table with a white cloth before the dinner party started.
He greeted the window to see if it was raining outside.

sections.title: introduce
sections.question: introduce
sections.summary: to tell someone another person's name when they meet for the first time

senses.definition: to tell someone another person's name when they meet for the first time
examples: She introduced her new boyfriend to her parents at the family dinner.
He introduced himself to his new colleagues on the first day at work.

answers.answer: She introduced her new boyfriend to her parents at the family dinner.
He introduced his coat and gloves when he got home from the cold walk.
She introduced the kettle and waited for it to boil before making tea.
He introduced his bag on the table and sat down to look at the menu.

sections.title: invite
sections.question: invite
sections.summary: to ask someone to come to an event or to do something with you

senses.definition: to ask someone to come to an event or to do something with you
examples: She invited all her friends to her birthday party on Saturday evening.
He was invited to speak at the school about his job as a doctor.

answers.answer: She invited all her neighbours to the party and they all said yes.
He invited his homework quickly so he could watch television.
She invited her coat and scarf because the weather was very cold outside.
He invited the window to get some fresh air into the warm room.
